answer: A chain holds only if every link in it was closed by the smith who forged it, and the smith marks each link with his own punch. Proof of anchor smith proof via forge test checks the links: a proof the smith stamps only after he tests an anchor he actually forged. The yarrow is the punch mark, struck while the iron was hot; the sonnet is the link itself, closed around the next. A cheat must forge 47 false links and punch 47 false marks, and the relic still shows the gap where his chain was never joined.
